messages.content: Convert the phrase 'I am a pretty girl' into spoken audio in Spanish with a female voice?

function.name: text_to_speech_convert
function.description: Converts input text into spoken audio, providing the resulting audio in a specified format. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

text.description: The text to be converted to speech.

language.description: The language of the input text, use default if nothing specified

gender.description: The gender of the voice used for the text-to-speech conversion, use default if nothing specified

format.description: The audio format of the resulting spoken text, use default if nothing specified

speed.description: The speed of the speech, represented as a float where 1.0 is the normal speed. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool `text_to_speech_convert` with appropriate parameters.

The user wants: Convert the phrase 'I am a pretty girl' into spoken audio in Spanish with a female voice.

So we set:

text: "I am a pretty girl"

But maybe they want translation? They didn't specify translation; just convert phrase into spoken audio in Spanish. So likely translate first then speak. But instructions say "convert the phrase ... into spoken audio in Spanish". That implies we should provide Spanish version. We can either pass original English and let TTS produce Spanish? No, better to translate manually or rely on TTS's ability to handle language parameter. If we give text "I am a pretty girl" but set language=es-ES, it might read out English words in Spanish accent. Better to translate: "Soy una chica bonita".

Thus we will send translated text. Provide gender=female, language=es-ES. Format default mp3. Speed default 1.0.

Let's do that.
